Chengdu成都

Cheapest tier-one lifestyle in the country, and a real foreign community.

Median asking
¥15k–35k/m²
Gross yield
2.6%–3.2%
Purchase cap
One self-use home
Land term
70 years, residential

Chengdu has the lowest entry price of any major Chinese city with genuine international amenities, and a reputation for a slower, more sociable pace of life that attracts long-stay foreigners rather than transient postings.

The foreign community is small but rooted: consulates, universities, a growing technology sector, and a food and café culture that does a lot of the integration work.

Can a foreigner buy here?

One self-use home, one year of work or study in Chengdu, purchase inside the city, valid residence permit and employment proof. Chengdu has been more relaxed than the coastal tier-one cities on enforcement detail, but the national framework still applies.

Jinjiang and Wuhou for central life, Gaoxin for newer stock and technology employers.

Before you view anything here

The paragraph above is a summary, not an answer. City practice is applied at district level and changes without much notice.

Take it to the counter: ask the district housing bureau to confirm your eligibility in writing, using the script in how to verify.

How to check it

Where to live

Districts that work for foreign buyers

Not every district is workable at every stage. These are the ones with the schools, services and resale liquidity foreigners actually need.

Jinjiang锦江

Central, walkable, the most established foreign-friendly neighbourhoods and services.

Wuhou武侯

Consulates, universities, good stock in the mid-range.

Gaoxin高新

Technology employers, newer buildings, younger buyer pool.

Tianfu New Area天府新区

Long-horizon infrastructure bet; large supply, thinner current services.

The market

How Chengdu actually trades

Supply is broad and prices are moderate. The risk is not price level but oversupply in the new districts, which can leave resale liquidity thin for a decade.

Living here

Settling in

Two airports, a growing metro, excellent food, and the lowest cost of living of any city on this list. Winter is damp and grey; summers are hot.

Know before you offer

Three risks in this market

  • Oversupply in peripheral new districts suppresses resale liquidity.
  • Fewer English-speaking lawyers and notaries than in Shanghai or Beijing.
  • Air quality is better than it was, but still variable in winter.

Best suited to

Long-stay buyers who prioritise lifestyle and cost over liquidity, and remote workers.

Structure of a deal

What a purchase in Chengdu actually looks like

Price is the last thing that decides the outcome. These four decide it first, and every one of them can be checked before you sign anything.

Who is on the other side

The marginal buyer is a local upgrader, and the foreign component is small and long-stay rather than corporate. Your exit therefore depends on local incomes, not on the expatriate rental market that made the city attractive.

What actually trades

Supply is broad and cheap by coastal standards. Oversupply in the new districts is the structural fact of this market, and it is the thing that will price your resale when you come to sell.

What is normal to negotiate

Prices are genuinely negotiable and the seller's holding cost is low, so patience works in your favour. Check the maintenance fund payment and the 满二/满五 status, because they move the total cost more than a small discount does.

What your exit looks like

In Tianfu and the outer new districts, resale can take a year or more and still fail. Buy where people already live, not where the masterplan says they will live in ten years.

The four words a city is argued in

  • 限购Purchase restriction
  • 学区School catchment
  • 契税Deed tax
  • 满五唯一Five years, only home
